messages.text: Not sure

You're in Poland around 20¢, so I'll use that. The B.1 is off sale until BitFortun ships its firmware fix — I can put you on the notify list for it.

Given your spare power, the Thor X1 still fits best: $219, 3.2 TH/s on ~25 W, about $3.60 a month to run.

Want me to build that cart?
Thor X1 is wifi only?
Searched the catalog · Thor X1 miner

Yes — Thor X1 is 2.4 GHz WiFi only, no ethernet port. If you want ethernet, the BC04 you already have has both.

One other thing worth knowing: the X1 ships without a power supply, it runs off USB-C, so you'd use a charger you already have.

Still want it in the cart?
Never wanted it in the first place.

Fair enough — dropping it.

You were on the BS-1 page, so: what pulled you to that one over the BC04 you're already running?
I'm not running it yet.

Got it — you have it but it's not plugged in yet.

What's stopping you, the setup or the power draw?
The setup.

It's a 10-minute job, honestly. Plug it in, it puts out its own WiFi network, you join that from your phone, give it your home WiFi, then paste in a pool address and your Bitcoin wallet address. That's the whole setup.

Where does it go wrong for you — the WiFi step, or picking a pool?
The wifi step.

Easiest fix: skip WiFi. The B.04 has an ethernet port — plug it straight into your router and it's on the network, no WiFi setup at all.

If you'd rather use WiFi, the usual culprit is the band: the BC04 only sees 2.4 GHz, so a combined 2.4/5 GHz network often won't show up for it.

Ethernet reachable where it'll sit?
Ethernet is reachable where it sits. But router is already full. No empty ports available.

Two ways round it. A five-port gigabit switch costs about 15 bucks at any electronics shop — unplug one device into the switch, and you get three spare ports back.

Or fix the WiFi side: in your router settings, split the bands or make a 2.4 GHz-only guest network, and the BC04 will see it.

Which sounds less annoying to you?
A five-port gigabit switch is better for me. But I'm looking at 24 or even 48 port switch from second hand. I have budget of 70 bucks.

Don't. A secondhand 24 or 48-port is rack gear — screaming fans and 30 to 50 W idle, 24/7. That's half a BC04's draw burned on nothing, in a room you have to live in.

A new 5-port is silent, fanless, about 2 W, and $15. Keeps $55 of your budget free.
I don't live at my attic where router is placed by installators.

Fair — then noise doesn't matter. The power still does, though: you told me you don't have headroom for a second BC04, and a 48-port idles at roughly the same draw as one.

For one miner you need one spare port. The 5-port does that for $15 and 2 W.
Great, I don't have headroom for second BC04 but I'm counting it with switch I don't already have yet.

Exactly right, and that's the argument for the small one. At your ~20¢, a 48-port at 50 W costs about $7.20 a month; the 5-port at 2 W costs about 29 cents.

Same job for one miner. Spend the headroom on hashrate, not on ports you'll never fill.
I will fill rather quicker than never.

Then go 8 or 16-port, unmanaged and fanless — still a few watts, still cheap, and you won't outgrow it. The 48-port rack units are the ones that burn power.

What's the plan you're wiring for — more miners, or other gear too?
will see when it will bring me profit. I'm planning to set it up on MiningDutch.

At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. What you get is a real piece of the network running in your own house, sats landing in your own wallet, no exchange, no KYC.

MiningDutch works fine for the BC04. Set it up, see the first payout, then decide on the switch.
What should I do. I already have an account there. But never mined anything on any ASIC.

Order of operations: get it on the network first, then point it at the pool.

On MiningDutch, grab the SHA-256 stratum address and port from their pool page. In the miner's web page, that goes in as the pool URL, the worker is yourusername.bc04, password x. Set the payout coin to BTC in your account.

Then just watch for your first accepted share.
I want to ask about a swich that drops no packets and is as close to 1ms ping as possible. Under 70 bucks is there any out there?

Any gigabit unmanaged switch does that. Store-and-forward adds about 5 microseconds per hop and drops nothing unless you're saturating a link — one miner sends a few shares a minute.

Your ping to the pool is your ISP's doing, not the switch's. Anything in the $15 to $40 range is already past the point where it matters.
What is my ISP's doing? How to check it?

From a PC on the same network, open a terminal and run `ping <pool hostname>` and then `tracert <pool hostname>`. Ping gives you the round trip; tracert shows where the delay appears — the first hop is your router, the second is your ISP.

From Poland to a Dutch pool you'd expect roughly 20 to 40 ms. Stale shares only start biting well above that.
20ms is too much. 40 is fatal.

It isn't, honestly. A share is only wasted if a new block lands during the round trip — that's 40 ms out of a 600-second block, about 0.007% of your shares. You'd lose roughly one share in fifteen thousand.

Gaming instinct, wrong sport. Big farms chase latency because they run petahashes; you're running 6 TH/s.
That one ishare lost is my winning reward.

I get it, and that's the right instinct — but you can't cut 40 ms to zero, you can only add tickets. Going from 6 to 12 TH/s doubles your draws; shaving latency buys you 0.007%.

Spend the $70 on the switch and keep the rest toward hashrate when the power headroom shows up.
I want to cut only to 5ms, not to 0.

Can't be done to a Dutch server: round trip Poland to Netherlands is about 1,100 km each way, and light in fibre does ~200 km/ms. That's 11 ms minimum, before any router touches it.

5 ms means a server inside Poland or just over the border. Pick the pool's nearest region if they offer one — that's your only real lever.
11 ms is good enough.

Good — then you're already there. Real-world you'll see 15 to 25 ms, which is the fibre plus a couple of hops, and that's fine.

Nothing left blocking you but a spare port. Grab an 8-port fanless switch, plug the BC04 in, point it at MiningDutch, and you're mining this weekend.
What is wrong with managed switch, that unmanaged is better?

Nothing's wrong with it — it's just features you don't need yet. VLANs, port monitoring, QoS, link aggregation. Costs more, draws a bit more, and you have to configure it.

If you want to watch per-port traffic on your miners later, a small managed one is genuinely nice. For getting one BC04 online, it's spend with no return.
What is the name of small managed one that is genuinely nice? Any recommendations?

We don't sell them, so take this as a mate's tip rather than a quote: the TP-Link TL-SG108E and Netgear GS308E are the usual 8-port fanless smart switches, around $30 to $40. MikroTik is widely stocked in Poland too and gives you far more to play with.

Check local pricing — I can't see those listings.
You're a great mate!
Used the chat-interview skill
Before you go, one thing: you've had the BC04 a while without plugging it in — what made it sit that long?
Already full router. No place for new cable. I have bought miner in the first place. And as a second move I want to buy something to connect it to with cable.
Makes sense. What made you order the miner before checking you had a port for it — was the ethernet part something you only hit once it arrived?
I wanted to buy Hammer Miner while it is available. Not when they all are sold. Switch I can buy always, miners seem to vanish quicker.
Fair read, honestly. What gave you that impression — did you watch something you wanted sell out first?
All I have is impressions and intuition.

That's a useful answer — thanks for the honesty.

Go get that switch, plug the BC04 in, and you'll have shares landing this weekend. Shout if the pool config gives you trouble.
Dziękuję.
Proszę bardzo. Good luck with the first shares.
Although I can say a word about the stand of this BC04. It is printed on a 3d printer, right?

Our BC04 listing only includes the miner, the 120 W supply and the cord — no stand, so I can't tell you what yours is from here. The N. S1 is the one that ships with a printed stand.

What does it look like, layer lines on it?
layer lines on it and fibers like hairs stand out.

Then yes, FDM printed — the hairs are stringing, purely cosmetic. A lighter wipes them off in seconds, or just pick them away.

One real thing: if it's PLA it softens around 60 °C, so keep the stand out of the exhaust path. PETG or ABS doesn't care.
It will certainly reach 61 degrees Celsius.

The heatsink will, sure. The stand sits at the base where it's much cooler, so in practice it's fine — but if you see it sag or lean after a week, that's your answer.

Easy fix either way: reprint it in PETG, or stand the unit on anything non-flammable.
I have found switch Switch Netgear ProSafe Plus GS116Ev2

Good find. Sixteen gigabit ports, fanless, metal case, and it idles low — well under the rack-switch figures we were worried about. VLANs and per-port stats if you ever want them, and it works fine untouched out of the box.

Plenty of room for miners two and three.
